summary: SWE-WebDev Bench is a 68-metric framework for 'vibe coding' app-builder platforms. It evaluates six commercial platforms (Base44, Emergent, Lovable, QwikBuild, Replit, v0) on three app-creation prompts (EdTech, field service, fintech-AI) seeded with 80 'canary' requirements and deliberate contradictions; app-modification prompts were run on QwikBuild only. Two of the three authors work for QwikBuild, which tops the engineering score (54.5%) and every requirement-elicitation metric and asks the most clarifying questions (15 on the vague prompt). Scoring was unblinded over 18 single-run cells with no statistics.

claims.claim: A specification bottleneck: platforms compress rich requirements, with Canary Retention 17.7-97.7% and Inference Quality 20-70
claims.evidence: Table 8 and Fig. 6 give per-platform PM diagnostics; scored by evaluators who knew the platform identity, including affiliated authors; n=3 prompts, one run each, no CIs (§5 statistical note, §7.6).

claims.claim: The degree of upstream planning strongly predicts downstream quality
claims.evidence: No correlation or regression between elicitation metrics and engineering score is reported; the same section notes the most thorough elicitor has the lowest code hygiene among top platforms and below-average external service reliability.

claims.claim: Requirement elicitation alone accounts for about 10-15% of the quality gap; build-time planning-execution feedback accounts for more
claims.evidence: Asserted in §5.2 and §7.2 with no decomposition, model or table anywhere in the body. The feedback-loop evidence is single-platform AMR data from the affiliated platform, which the authors say cannot support causal claims.

claims.claim: No platform exceeds 60% engineering score or 65% security score
claims.evidence: Tables 5-6. About 40% of the engineering score is from automated tools (Lighthouse, k6, npm audit); the rest uses LLM judges and panels; metric weights and targets are author-chosen ('practitioner consensus from the authors' experience operating a production AI app platform').

claims.claim: All platforms catch a marked contradiction, but only one detects an unmarked one
claims.evidence: Table 9 (marked P2 contradiction: 6/6 detected, 3 resolved by asking) and §5.2.3 (unmarked P1 contradiction: one platform, implied to be QwikBuild in App. B). One trial per platform.

patterns.note: The platform with a dedicated PM agent asking 15 structured multiple-choice clarifying questions (QwikBuild) leads Explicit Capture (93.7%), Inference Quality (70) and canary retention, while zero-question platforms (Replit, Base44) score low on these. This is a confounded cross-platform comparison (every architecture differs), scored unblinded by affiliated authors over 3 prompts; the paper also says elicitation explains only an unanalysed '10-15%' of the gap. No isolating comparison of asking vs not asking.
The affiliated platform's 12-section PRD includes acceptance criteria and open questions, and canary requirements serve as checkable acceptance details. Neither is isolated.
'Proactive Discovery Rate' and 'Conversational Guidance' diagnostics score requirement exploration from transcripts; no outcome comparison of discovery approaches.

Argues multi-agent closed-loop planning and execution beats single-pass generation, based on the affiliated platform's AMR data (100% change acknowledgement, Table 15); authors concede it needs independent cross-platform validation.
Claude 3.5 Sonnet judge for Tier-1/2 metrics: kappa 0.82 on 36 items and 0.71 on 18 items, both below the paper's own targets (0.85, 0.75); expert panel kappa 0.64.

methodology.sample: 6 platforms x 3 app-creation prompts = 18 cells, one run each; 3 modification prompts on QwikBuild only; 80 canary requirements; Feb-Mar 2026 snapshot
methodology.baselines: Cross-platform only; no human-built reference application or non-platform agent
methodology.models: Commercial platforms with uncontrolled underlying models; judge Claude 3.5 Sonnet at T=0
methodology.variance: None; authors state no significance tests or CIs and estimate 15-20 prompts would be needed
methodology.contamination_controls: Canaries and AMR prompts designed by the non-affiliated author; evaluators not blinded
methodology.languages: Full-stack web apps in platform-chosen stacks (mostly TypeScript/JavaScript)

standards.artifacts: Prompts, canary specs, 9 judge templates, raw CSV scores and anonymization scripts claimed at github.com/snowmountainAi/webdevbench

biases.detail: Affiliated authors scored their own platform, which ranks first on engineering score and every PM metric, without blinding (§7.6).
Three creation prompts per platform; 18 cells total; modification only on one platform.
One run per cell on stochastic commercial platforms.
Judge agreement measured on 18-36 items and below the paper's own targets.
'Virtual software agency', 'strongly predicts', 'first benchmark to...' framing beyond what n=18 supports.
Authors concede the emphasis on PM elicitation and canary retention may structurally advantage platforms with a dedicated PM agent, the affiliated platform's differentiator.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: QwikBuild (affiliated) plus Base44, Emergent, Lovable, Replit, v0
coi.detail: Vendor authors grade their own platform favorably without blinding or independent replication, and the modification track covers only the affiliated platform. Disclosure and partial mitigations (non-affiliated canary author, released rubrics, reporting some QwikBuild weaknesses) do not offset this.

verdict_reason: Vendor-graded and unblinded, with 18 single-run cells and no statistics; the headline causal statements ('strongly predicts', the 10-15% elicitation share) are never computed in the body. The deterministic gate rejects it as well (high COI with rigor 2).
applicability: The evidence does not transfer: consumer app builders, unblinded vendor scoring. Two test techniques are worth trying independently in the team's discovery harness: (1) canary requirements, where domain-specific details (for example healthcare-education content conventions or accreditation rules) are seeded into a request and checked for survival into the spec and the code; (2) an unmarked-contradiction probe that checks whether the clarification step surfaces conflicts instead of silently choosing one. Use them as harness tests, not as evidence that clarifying-question agents work.

conflicts_with.detail: SWE-RPG finds implicit-requirement recovery is the most common failure stage (24.5-46% of runs) for coding agents; this paper asserts, without analysis, that requirement elicitation explains only about 10-15% of the quality gap and that build-time feedback matters more.

Mise en Place prescribes completing all preparation before implementation; this paper argues closed-loop planning-execution feedback matters more than any upfront phase. Neither has controlled evidence.
